why: Count the layers on one shared axis: 29 sets on 4 lanes with bars sized to real minutes, 9 hour ticks, 2 road windows a day and a 241-point tide curve against a dashed 2.4 ft line; note that a connected 4-stop rail is the tab control, the hover cursor reads time, tide height, road state and the set on stage while lighting that set, and each panel ends in three plain facts a visitor can act on (arrive by 1:33 pm, earliest way home 10:28 pm).

The price chip is the only thing that fills on selection, and choosing a ticket rewrites a whole ruled order row: name, quantity clamped 1 to 8, computed total, and a Friday, Saturday, Sunday picker that exists only for the One day ticket; the tier rule (Tier 2 of 3, $30 more on February 1 or after 1,100 passes) sits in the heading and "There is no VIP ticket" in the fine print, so the pricing states its logic without any feature ticks.

27 rows each hide a stage, a hometown and one sentence specific to that act; the trick to copy is a fixed list height plus flex-grow 4.84, so the open row takes 156px while eight closed rows tighten from 46px to about 32px and nothing below the list moves, with hierarchy from only three levels: 13px muted tabular time, 16px name, 15px note.

8 icons drawn from rects on the same 28px tile as the logo, 8 answers that each carry something a visitor can plan around ($10 a day, $38 each way, 12 people at a time, 16 stairs), exclusive groups through native details[name], and a printed card with 8 rows of road windows as the proof object: three columns holding different content on one ruled grid, with no script.

Nav, signup block and footer sit on one ruled grid, so the six nav cells and the full-cell CTA line up with the footer columns below; notice that live data replaces decoration: one tide function fills the corner tray status, the next low water in the legal row and the phone menu line, the logo crossbar moves with scroll, and the page closes on a 96px sentence stating a fact about the road.
